reddit.purpose: Normalize Reddit posts, comments, actors, communities, timestamps, links and delivery metrics into CCE evidence/context records.
reddit.dynamic_space_rule: A space is a runtime context value. Adding or changing a subreddit never creates a new Reddit adapter version.

hearingtracker_forum.purpose: Normalize forum.hearingtracker.com (Discourse) topics, posts, actors, timestamps and links into CCE evidence/context records.
hearingtracker_forum.dynamic_space_rule: A topic is a runtime context value. Adding or changing a topic never creates a new adapter version.

quora.purpose: Normalize Quora questions, answers, actors, topics, timestamps and links into CCE evidence/context records.
quora.dynamic_space_rule: A question or topic is a runtime context value. Adding or changing one never creates a new adapter version.

instagram.purpose: Normalize Instagram profiles, feed posts, carousels, captions, hashtags, image/visual descriptors, bio-link state, actors, timestamps and delivery metrics into CCE evidence/context records. Protocol facts this adapter encodes: the image is the primary readout surface and the caption is subordinate to it; captions carry no clickable links (link lives in bio and must be declared as bio_link state); discovery is hashtag- and explore-driven; audience scans visually before reading.
instagram.dynamic_space_rule: A profile or post shortcode is a runtime context value. Adding or changing one never creates a new Instagram adapter version.

facebook.purpose: Normalize Facebook Page posts, link previews, captions, actors, page identity fields, timestamps and delivery metrics into CCE evidence/context records. Protocol facts this adapter encodes: feed posts carry clickable links with an auto-generated preview card; the audience skews older and mixed-intent (consumer and trade) and reads Page identity (name, category, address) as trust signals; long-form narrative posts are native to the surface; reshares and comments are the delivery mechanism.
facebook.dynamic_space_rule: A page id or post id is a runtime context value. Adding or changing one never creates a new Facebook adapter version.

threads.purpose: Normalize Threads profiles, text-first posts, reply chains, actors, timestamps and delivery metrics into CCE evidence/context records. Protocol facts this adapter encodes: hard 500-character limit with silent truncation (overflow is destroyed, not clipped visibly); the surface is conversational and text-first with optional attached media; the audience expects a spoken-register opinion or observation, not an announcement; a small number of hashtags (about three) aids distribution; links are clickable but de-emphasized by the feed.
threads.dynamic_space_rule: A profile or post is a runtime context value. Adding or changing one never creates a new Threads adapter version.

x.purpose: Normalize X (Twitter) profiles, single posts, quote/reply chains, actors, timestamps, link wrapping and delivery metrics into CCE evidence/context records. Protocol facts this adapter encodes: 280-character limit with every URL wrapped to a fixed 23-character t.co token; the feed is fast-scroll and headline-driven, industry and B2B actors are native; the audience expects one anchored claim with a number and a link, digressions are skipped; media attaches without consuming characters.
x.dynamic_space_rule: A profile or status id is a runtime context value. Adding or changing one never creates a new X adapter version.

owned_site.purpose: Normalize copy published on a surface the speaker owns (marketing site, docs, landing page) into CCE evidence/context records. Unlike platform adapters there is no feed, no community norm and no ephemerality: the text is persistent, self-hosted and cross-checkable against sibling pages, so the burden of proof sits entirely with the speaker.
owned_site.dynamic_space_rule: A page path is a runtime context value. Adding or changing a page never creates a new adapter version.

protocol_facts.distribution: none — the reader arrives with intent, usually from search or a direct link, not from an algorithmic feed
protocol_facts.norm_source: regulation and the speaker's own published commitments, not community rules
protocol_facts.persistence: permanent and re-readable; wording can be quoted back and compared verbatim across visits
protocol_facts.authorship: the speaker owns the surface, so nothing is moderated away and every claim is attributable
protocol_facts.cross_surface_check: the reader can open sibling pages in the same visit — a claim that contradicts another page on the same domain fails here in a way it would not on a feed
